intro:
# Granite Manager — User Manual (Feature Map)

This document is a high-level map of what the application offers, organized by user role and navigation area. It is derived from the app’s routes, sidebar navigation, and page components.

Granite Manager is an AI-powered CRM and inventory platform built for countertop and stone fabrication shops. It connects customer relationships, deal pipelines, stone/slab inventory, communications, and back-office operations in one system.

---

## Admin Company Settings & Users

These pages configure your company profile and staff accounts. They live under the **Company settings** section in the Admin sidebar (collapsible group with a building icon). You need **Admin** access plus the **Manager** position (platform superusers always have access). The **Super Admin** position alone is not enough: Super Admins also need Manager, which only applies in their home company. Other admins without Manager do not see **Company settings** at all.

#### How to reach these pages (sidebar path + route)

| Page | Sidebar navigation | Route | Page title (heading) |
|------|-------------------|-------|----------------------|
| **Company** (logo, name, tax) | **Admin** view → **Company settings** → **Company** | `/admin/company` | **Company** |
| **Users** (staff list) | **Admin** view → **Company settings** → **Users** | `/admin/users` | **Users** |

Switch to the **Admin** portal from the sidebar header (toggle **Employee** / **Admin**) before following the paths above.

---

### Company page (`/admin/company`)

**Page title:** Company

**What you see:** A white card form (`max-width` panel with light shadow) containing company fields. There is no separate “branding” page — the logo is the **Logo** field on this form.

Use this page to update how your company appears in the app header and on customer-facing pages.

#### Adding or changing the company logo

1. Sign in as an admin with the **Manager** position.
2. Switch to **Admin** view in the sidebar header.
3. In the sidebar, click **Company settings** to expand the section (building icon + chevron).
4. Click **Company** (sub-item under Company settings). URL: `/admin/company`.
5. On the **Company** page, scroll to the **Logo** section (below **Company address**, above **Sales Tax (%)**).
6. Under the **Logo** label:
   - If a logo already exists, you see a **preview** in a dashed border box (centered image).
   - Adjust **Logo height** with the slider (label shows **Logo height** and current value in px, e.g. **48px**; range **32px–192px**).
   - Click the **file input** (standard browser file chooser) and select an image: PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, or SVG. Large images are resized automatically on upload.
7. Click **Save** at the bottom of the form.
8. Success toast: **Company settings saved**. The logo appears in the app **header** (top bar) at the height you set.

To keep the existing logo file, do not choose a new file — only change **Logo height** or other fields, then **Save**.

#### All fields on the Company form

| Field label (exact UI text) | Required? | Rules and notes |
|----------------------------|-----------|-----------------|
| **Company name** | Yes | Placeholder: **Company name**. Shown across the app and in customer emails. |
| **Company address** | No | Label: **Company address**. Address autocomplete field. |
| **Logo** | No | Label: **Logo**. Preview + **Logo height** slider + file upload. Not called “branding” in the UI. |
| **Sales Tax (%)** | No | Placeholder example: **7**. Used by **Special Order** and other pricing. Range 0–100. Configurable only by users with the **Manager** position and **Admin** access. |
| **Company ID : {number}** | Display only | Read-only ID below the tax field. |

Click **Save** (loading state while submitting). Success toast: **Company settings saved**.

If you lack permission, opening `/admin/company` redirects to login with an invalid-permissions error.

**Not the company logo:** Stone catalog photos are **Main photo** on **Admin → Inventory → Stones** — a different feature entirely.

---

### Users list (`/admin/users`)

**Page title:** Users

#### Table columns

| Column | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **Name*** | Staff display name |
| **Email** | Login email (may be empty for some accounts) |
| **Phone Number** | Contact phone |
| **CloudTalk Agent ID** | Links CRM user to CloudTalk for calls/SMS activity |
| **CloudTalk Phone** | CloudTalk line used as SMS sender for this user |
| **Actions** | **Edit** menu (when you have edit permission) |

#### Who can do what

| Action | Who |
|--------|-----|
| **View** the user list | Admins with Manager, and platform superusers |
| **Edit** a user | Same as above — opens the edit dialog. Platform superuser and **Super Admin** accounts can only be edited by a platform superuser; for anyone else their row has no **Actions** menu. |
| **Add User** | Admins with Manager, and platform superusers — button at top left |
| **Delete** a user | **Platform superusers only** — soft-delete via actions menu |
| **Filter by company** | **Platform superusers only** — company dropdown above the table |

Company managers see only users in their own company. Platform superusers can switch **All companies** or one company via `?companyId=` in the URL.

---

### Add user (`/admin/users/add`)

Opens as a dialog from the Users page.

| Field | Required? | Notes |
|-------|-----------|-------|
| **User Name** | Yes | |
| **Phone Number** | No | Minimum 10 digits when provided |
| **Email** | No | Must be valid if provided |
| **Password** | Yes | Minimum 4 characters |
| **Company** | Yes | Which company the user belongs to |
| **Positions** | No | Toggle switches for each position (Sales Representative, Installer, Shop Worker, etc.). Hover/info icons describe each role. A user can't be both **Sales Representative** and **Shop Worker**: turning one on turns the other off. |
| **Admin** | No | When on, user can access Admin portal |

Click **Save changes** to create the user. New accounts are marked as employees.

---

### Edit user (`/admin/users/edit/:userId`)

Opens as a dialog from the row **Actions → Edit** menu.

#### Basic fields

| Field | Editable by |
|-------|-------------|
| **Name**, **Phone**, **Email** | Managers and platform superusers |
| **Company** | Platform superuser only (managers see a hidden fixed company) |
| **CloudTalk agent ID** | Managers and platform superusers — required for SMS from CRM and for **Made a call** in Users Activity. Get the ID on [cloudtalk.io](https://cloudtalk.io) (Users → click user → number at end of URL), then enter it on **My Account** (`/employee/user`) or **Admin → Users → Edit**. |
| **CloudTalk phone number** | Managers and platform superusers — the outbound SMS line for this user. At least 10 digits when set. |
| **Positions** | Toggle each position on/off. Managers cannot assign or remove **Super Admin** or **Walk-in** (superusers manage those). A user can't be both **Sales Representative** and **Shop Worker**. |
| **Admin** | Managers and platform superusers |

#### Connect a CRM user to CloudTalk

Only a **CloudTalk Admin** can open and edit CloudTalk user settings and obtain the Agent ID from the user-edit URL. If you are not a CloudTalk Admin, ask your company’s CloudTalk Admin to provide the Agent ID and assigned phone number.

Use both steps below: first get the ID from CloudTalk, then enter it in the CRM.

##### Option 1: Get the Agent ID on CloudTalk.io

1. Go to [cloudtalk.io](https://cloudtalk.io) and log in with a **CloudTalk Admin** account.
2. Open **Users**. In older CloudTalk versions, this area may be labeled **Agents**.
3. Use the search field to search for the agent by name or email.
4. Click the matching user to open their edit page.
5. Look at the browser address bar. The **Agent ID** is the number at the very end of the URL.

##### Option 2: Enter the Agent ID in the CRM

**My Account** (the user enters their own ID):

1. Open sidebar **My Account** → `/employee/user` (Employee) or `/shop/user` (Shop).
2. In **Personal Information**, paste the ID into **CloudTalk agent ID**.
3. Click **Save**.

**Admin → Users** (a Manager or platform superuser enters it for someone else):

1. Switch to the **Admin** portal.
2. Open **Company settings → Users**.
3. Find the CRM user and select **Actions → Edit**.
4. Paste the ID into **CloudTalk agent ID** (and set **CloudTalk phone number** if needed).
5. Click **Save**.

The Agent ID links the correct CloudTalk agent to the correct CRM user. Granite Manager needs it to load that user’s CloudTalk calls and show **Made a call** records under **Admin → Users Activity**.

##### Find the CloudTalk phone number

1. In the CloudTalk Dashboard, open **Numbers**.
2. Use the search field to find the assigned number. You can search by the phone number or identify it from the agent’s assigned numbers in **Users → Edit user**.
3. Copy the complete CloudTalk number, including country code.
4. Paste it into **CloudTalk phone number** in the Granite Manager user editor.

The CloudTalk phone number is the outbound line Granite Manager uses when that user sends SMS. It is also used for automated SMS workflows, such as sending a post-install survey from the Office Manager’s configured CloudTalk line. Enter at least 10 digits.

The two fields serve different purposes:

| Field | Why Granite Manager needs it |
|-------|------------------------------|
| **CloudTalk agent ID** | Matches call history to the CRM user and enables **Made a call** activity. |
| **CloudTalk phone number** | Selects the CloudTalk line used to send SMS from the CRM. |

#### Position side panels

- **External Marketing Companies** — When **Marketing** position is enabled, choose which companies the marketer can access.
- **Super Admin Companies** — When **Super Admin** position is enabled (superuser editor only), choose which companies the super admin can switch to.

Enabling **Super Admin** position automatically sets **Admin** on.

Click **Save** to update. Success toast: **User updated**.

#### Change a person's name (installer, sales rep, technician, shop worker)

Every staff name in the app comes from that person's user account. There is no separate installer name, sales rep name, or technician name field anywhere else — renaming the user renames them everywhere.

1. Go to **Admin → Company settings → Users**.
2. Find the person in the table (Super Admins can switch company with the company dropdown first).
3. Open **Actions → Edit** on that row.
4. Change the **Name** field.
5. Click **Save**. Success toast: **User updated**.

**Who can do it:** a **Manager** with Admin access, or a **Super Admin**. Managers can rename anyone in their own company, including installers — adding or removing the **Super Admin** position is the only part reserved for superusers.

The new name then shows everywhere that person appears, such as the **Survey** cards, checklist records, the survey **Pick your sales rep** and **Pick your installer** dropdowns, Users Activity, and deal or customer assignment lists. Surveys and checklists already submitted keep the name that was stored when they were saved.

---

### Delete user (`/admin/users/delete/:userId`) — Super Admin only

Soft-deletes the user (`is_deleted = 1`). The account no longer appears in lists but historical records may still reference the name.

---

### How positions affect surveys and activity

| Position | Relevant to |
|----------|-------------|
| **Sales Representative** | Appears in customer survey dropdown; listed in Users Activity rep grid |
| **Installer** | Appears in customer survey installer dropdown |
| **Office Manager** | CloudTalk phone used to SMS survey link after checklist submit |
| **Manager** | Unlocks **Company settings** sidebar section (**Users** and **Company**) with Admin login |
| **Super Admin** | Add/delete users, switch companies, assign super-admin company access |

Position descriptions are shown next to each toggle in Add/Edit user dialogs.

---

### Typical workflow for office managers

1. **Company settings → Company** — Set legal name, address, logo, and sales tax once during onboarding; update tax when rates change.
2. **Users** — For each sales rep, set **CloudTalk agent ID** and phone so SMS and call tracking work.
3. Assign **Office Manager** to the staff member whose CloudTalk line should send post-install survey texts.
4. When hiring, ask a Super Admin to **Add User**, assign positions, then a Manager can **Edit** CloudTalk fields and fine-tune roles.

---

## Admin Deals (Deal Board — Admin View)

Admins use the same Kanban deal board as employees, but with a **company-wide, read-only overview** plus tools to configure the pipeline. Employees work their **own** deals day to day; admins **oversee all reps** and **set up** groups, stages, and email templates.

**Where to find it:** Sign in as Admin → sidebar **CRM** → **Deals**. Opens at `/admin/deals`.

For employee day-to-day deal workflow, see [Employee Deals (Deal Board & Pipeline)](#employee-deals-deal-board--pipeline).

---

### How Admin deals differ from Employee deals

| Topic | Employee (`/employee/deals`) | Admin (`/admin/deals`) |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------|
| **Whose deals** | Only deals owned by **you** (`user_id` = your account) | **All company deals** across sales reps |
| **Sales rep filter** | Not on the board (you only see yours) | **Sales Reps** dropdown — filter by rep name or **All** |
| **Group filter URL** | `?view=` (group id) | `?group=` (group id) |
| **Status filter** | Dropdown: Active / Won / Lost | **Menu** → Status Filter (same three options) |
| **Drag and drop** | Yes — move your deals between stages | **No** — board is **read-only** for moves |
| **Add Deal** | **Add Deal** button on toolbar | **Not available** on admin board |
| **Inline card edits** | Amount and activity deadline on cards | **Disabled** (read-only cards) |
| **Overdue group alert** | Red icon when another group has overdue tasks | Not shown on admin board |
| **Find Customer** | Search **your** deals; Edit/Delete shortcuts | Search **all** deals; row click disabled (use card link to open) |
| **Opening a deal** | Full edit: win/loss, email, activities | Open for **view and admin edits** — see below |
| **Manage pipeline** | Uses boards configured by admin | **Menu → Manage Lists**, **Manage Questionnaires**; email/SMS tools on **CRM → Automations** |

---

### Browsing the admin deal board

The layout matches the employee board: stage **columns**, deal **cards** with customer name, amount, activity, icons, and sales rep in the corner.

**Toolbar (left to right):**

1. **Sales Reps** — filter the whole board to one rep or show **All**.
2. **Group** — switch deal board layout (same groups employees see).
3. **Menu** (☰):
   - **Status Filter** — Active Deals, Won, Lost
   - **Manage Lists** — opens pipeline configuration
   - **Manage Questionnaires** — opens company questionnaire manager

Cards show which **sales rep** owns each deal. Click the **customer name** on a card to open **Edit Deal**.

You cannot drag deals or add deals from this screen. Stage changes for a deal happen when a rep moves it on the employee board, or when an admin updates the deal on the **General** tab (see below).

---

### Opening a deal (admin)

The **Edit Deal** dialog uses the same tabs and activity panel as employee deals:

- **Project** — **read-only** customer/project table (no Won/Lost buttons, no group switcher, no **Email** compose button on the email row). View contact data, map link, SMS on phone, attached files.
- **General** — edit **customer**, **amount**, **title**; **Save** or **Delete**. Updates apply to any rep’s deal (no `user_id` ownership check). Moving stage via saved `list_id` can reactivate a closed deal the same way as employee **General** save.
- **Files** — same image and document upload/manage behavior as employee.
- **Questionnaire** — same answer, save, create-note, and manage-questionnaire behavior as employee deals. See [Questionnaire tab](#questionnaire-tab) in Employee Deals.
- **Activity panel** — **Activity** and **Notes** tabs at the top; add/complete activities, add notes via **Add Note**, view history (including **Notes** tab). Same note workflow as employee deals.

Admins **do not** mark deals Won/Lost from the admin **Project** tab. Reps do that on `/employee/deals`. Admins can still see won/lost deals using the status filter and lost reason on cards.

---

### Manage Lists (`/admin/deals/manage-lists`)

Configure the pipeline employees use. Open from **Menu → Manage Lists**.

#### Deal groups

Each **group** is a separate board (e.g. Homeowners, Commercial). For each group:

| Control | What it does |
|---------|----------------|
| **Visible / Hidden** | Toggle whether the group appears in employee and admin group dropdowns |
| **Default / Assign leads here** | Mark one group as default for new auto-created deals |
| **Add Group** | Top-right form — name + **Add Group** |
| **Delete group** (trash) | Soft-deletes group and its lists (not allowed for built-in patterns on non-custom groups) |

**Default group** (id = 1): lists cannot be reordered or deleted; you can still toggle visibility.

#### Stage lists (columns)

Inside each group card:

- **Drag** lists by the grip handle to **reorder** columns on the board.
- **Add List** — type name + **Add List** (not available in Default group).
- **Delete list** (trash) — removes a stage column (not in Default group).

New deals from employees land in the first column of the active group unless otherwise specified.

---

### Email templates (`/admin/automations/email-templates`)

Open from the sidebar **CRM → Automations → Email Templates**.

- Browse company **email templates** used in compose and deal email flows.
- **Add**, **edit**, and **delete** templates.
- Search by template name.

Employees use these templates when sending mail from **Emails** or deal compose; admins maintain the library here.

---

### Manage Questionnaires (`/admin/deals/questionnaires`)

Open from **Menu → Manage Questionnaires**.

Use this screen to maintain discovery questionnaires for the company:

1. Click **Add Questionnaire**, enter a name, and create the questionnaire.
2. Open **Edit** to rename it and add, edit, or delete questions.
3. Use search to find an existing questionnaire by name.
4. Delete a questionnaire when it should no longer appear on deals.

Reps and admins can also manage questionnaires from a deal’s **Questionnaire** tab. If a deal has no questionnaires yet, the tab points staff to this admin menu entry.

---

### When to use Admin vs Employee deals

| Task | Use |
|------|-----|
| Work your own pipeline, drag deals, win/loss | **Employee** deals |
| See another rep’s board or whole team | **Admin** deals + Sales Rep filter |
| Add a new deal | **Employee** deals |
| Rename stages or add a group | **Admin** → Manage Lists |
| Fix deal amount/customer on any rep’s deal | **Admin** → open deal → **General** |
| Maintain email templates for sales | **Admin** → Email Templates |
| Create company questionnaires for discovery | **Admin** → Manage Questionnaires |

---

## Admin Instructions (Knowledge Base & Position Visibility)

Use **Instructions** to build your company's internal knowledge base: policies, pricing formulas, procedures, and reference material. Admins create and organize content; employees browse what their **position** allows them to see.

**Where to find it (Admin):** Sign in with **Admin** access → sidebar **Resources** → **Instructions**. Opens at `/admin/instructions`.

**Where employees see it:** Sidebar **Resources** → **Instructions** (`/employee/instructions`), and **AI Chat** in **Instructions** mode.

---

### Company vs General instructions

At the top of the page, tabs switch the instruction library:

| Tab | Who sees the tab | Contents |
|-----|------------------|----------|
| **Company instructions** | All admins; all employees | Your company's own instruction tree |
| **General instructions** | **Super Admin** only (admin page) | Shared instructions stored at company ID 0 |

Employees always see both **Company instructions** and **General instructions** tabs on their Instructions page.

---

### Browsing and managing (Admin view)

Admins see the **full** instruction tree — position restrictions do **not** hide items on the admin page.

| Control | What it does |
|---------|----------------|
| **Add Instruction** | Opens the create dialog |
| **Search instructions...** | Search by title or body text |
| **Pencil** icon on a row | Edit that instruction |
| **Trash** icon on a row | Delete that instruction |
| **Grip** handle | Drag to reorder siblings within the same parent |

---

### Adding an instruction

1. On **Admin** → **Resources** → **Instructions**, click **Add Instruction**.
2. The **Add instruction** dialog opens.
3. Fill in the form:

| Field label (exact UI text) | Required? | Notes |
|----------------------------|-----------|--------|
| **Title** | **Yes** | Placeholder: **Name of the instruction** |
| **Parent** | No | Place under an existing instruction in the tree, or leave as top-level |
| **After** | No | Insert after a sibling under the same parent |
| **Visible to** | No | Position access — see [Setting instruction position visibility](#setting-instruction-position-visibility) below. Default: **Everyone** |
| **Text** | No | Rich text body (Quill editor) |

4. Click **Add Instruction**.
5. Success toast: **Instruction added**. The dialog closes and the new item appears in the tree.

---

### Setting instruction position visibility

Each instruction has a **Visible to** control that limits which **staff positions** can read it on the employee Instructions page and in **AI Chat → Instructions** mode.

#### Where the control appears

- **Add instruction** dialog — below **Parent** / **After**, above **Text**
- **Edit Instruction** dialog — below **Title**, above **Text**

#### How to use it

1. Hover over the **Visible to** label (or focus it).
2. A panel opens with toggle switches — one per position.
3. Turn **on** every position that should see this instruction.
4. Save the instruction (**Add Instruction** or **Save changes**).

#### Summary line

Under **Visible to**, a gray summary shows the current setting:

| Summary text | Meaning |
|--------------|---------|
| **Everyone** | No position toggles are on — all employees can see this instruction |
| Comma-separated position names | Only users with **at least one** of those positions can see it |

Example summary: `Sales Representative, Shop Worker` — only users who have the Sales Representative position **or** the Shop Worker position (or both) will see this instruction.

#### Position toggles available

These positions appear in the **Visible to** panel:

| Toggle label | Position |
|--------------|----------|
| **Sales Representative** | Sales reps |
| **Sales Manager** | Sales managers |
| **Shop Manager** | Shop managers |
| **Shop Worker** | Shop workers |
| **Manager** | Managers |
| **Installer** | Installers |
| **Marketing** | Marketing staff |
| **Office Manager** | Office managers |
| **Template Guy** | Template technicians |

**Not in the panel:** **Super Admin** and **Walk-in** do not appear as toggles. They are excluded from per-instruction visibility settings.

#### How matching works

- **No toggles on (Everyone):** Every employee who can open **Resources → Instructions** sees the instruction.
- **One or more toggles on:** A user sees the instruction only if their account has **at least one** of the selected positions (from **Admin → Company settings → Users → Edit → Positions**).
- **Per instruction:** Visibility is set on each instruction individually. Child instructions do **not** automatically inherit a parent's **Visible to** setting — configure each item separately if needed.
- **Hidden from tree:** Restricted instructions are removed entirely from the employee instruction tree and from outline search results for users who lack a matching position.

#### Where position visibility applies

| Area | Filtered by position? |
|------|----------------------|
| **Employee → Instructions** | **Yes** |
| **AI Chat → Instructions** mode | **Yes** — the assistant only receives instructions visible to the signed-in user |
| **Admin → Instructions** | **No** — admins always see the full tree for editing |
| **Teach Mode** (employee or admin) | **No** — teach-mode instruction pickers load the full company tree regardless of **Visible to** settings |

---

### Editing an instruction

1. On the admin Instructions page, click the **pencil** icon on the instruction row (or use search to find it first).
2. The **Edit Instruction** dialog opens.
3. Update **Title**, **Visible to**, and/or **Text**.
4. Click **Save changes**.
5. Success toast: **Instruction updated**.

**Note:** **Parent** and **After** placement are preserved from when the instruction was created. Reorder siblings with drag-and-drop on the main admin page instead of changing parent in the edit dialog.

---

### Deleting an instruction

1. Click the **trash** icon on the instruction row.
2. Confirm in the delete dialog.

---

### Employee Instructions page

**Where to find it:** Sign in as Employee → sidebar **Resources** → **Instructions**.

Employees see only instructions their positions allow (see [How matching works](#how-matching-works) above).

| Feature | What it does |
|---------|----------------|
| **Company instructions** / **General instructions** tabs | Switch between company-specific and shared general content |
| Accordion tree | Expand sections to read rich text content |
| **Outline** panel (desktop) | Jump to a section; **Search...** finds titles and body text among **visible** instructions only |

Employees cannot add, edit, delete, or change **Visible to** settings.

---

### Typical workflows

**Restrict pricing procedures to sales staff**

1. **Admin → Instructions** → edit the pricing instruction (or **Add Instruction**).
2. Under **Visible to**, enable **Sales Representative** and **Sales Manager** only.
3. **Save changes**.
4. Shop workers and other positions no longer see that item on **Employee → Instructions** or in AI Chat Instructions mode.

**Make a procedure visible to everyone**

1. Open the instruction in **Edit Instruction**.
2. Under **Visible to**, turn **off** all position toggles so the summary reads **Everyone**.
3. **Save changes**.

**Onboard a new position**

1. **Admin → Company settings → Users** — assign the correct position(s) to the user.
2. Instructions with **Visible to** including that position become available automatically on their next visit.

---

### Tips

- Use **Everyone** for company-wide policies (safety, hours, general contact info).
- Restrict sensitive pricing or commission instructions to **Sales Representative** / **Sales Manager** only.
- After changing **Visible to**, ask a user with a different position to confirm they no longer see (or now see) the item under **Resources → Instructions**.
- **Teach Mode** quizzes are not position-filtered — if a quiz should align with restricted content, manage quiz visibility separately in **Admin → Teach Mode**.

## Admin portal (`/admin`)

Default landing: **Stones** (`/admin/stones`).

Admin includes nearly all Employee CRM and inventory features, plus configuration and reporting. Deal and customer edit flows mirror Employee routes under `/admin/deals` and `/admin/customers`.

Full step-by-step instructions for **Admin Deals** (and how they differ from Employee) are in [Admin Deals (Deal Board — Admin View)](#admin-deals-deal-board--admin-view) above.

Full step-by-step instructions for **Surveys**, **Users Activity**, and **Company / Users** are in [Admin Surveys (Customer Feedback)](#admin-surveys-customer-feedback), [Admin Users Activity (Sales Rep & Staff Tracking)](#admin-users-activity-sales-rep--staff-tracking), and [Admin Company Settings & Users](#admin-company-settings--users) below.

### Inventory management (Admin-only create/edit/delete)

Full step-by-step instructions for **Stones** are in [Admin Stones (Stone / Material Management)](#admin-stones-stone--material-management) below.

- **Sinks** — Add, edit, images, delete
- **Faucets** — Add, edit, images, delete
- **Supports** — Add, edit, delete corbel/support items

---

## Admin portal (other areas)

The following Admin areas are summarized here. Deal and stone workflows have dedicated sections above.

### Deals (`/admin/deals`)
- Company-wide read-only deal board with sales-rep filter
- **Manage Lists** and **Email templates** for pipeline setup
- See [Admin Deals (Deal Board — Admin View)](#admin-deals-deal-board--admin-view)

### Customers (`/admin/customers`)
- Full customer CRUD; same info modal pattern as Employee

### Emails (`/admin/emails`)
- Company-wide email view (Admin scope)
- Same **Mark as unread** / **Mark as read** actions as Employee Emails (Inbox row envelope, or toolbar after selecting threads)

### Statistics (`/admin/statistics`)
- Deals by sales rep: counts, amounts, win/loss ratios
- Filters by date range, customer, sales rep
- Breakdowns for walk-in vs leads sources

### Transactions (`/admin/transactions`)
- All company transactions; link to **Reports**

### Reports (`/admin/reports`)
- Slab cut/sale reports with filters (date, supplier, stone, seller)

### Surveys (`/admin/surveys`)
- Read-only list of customer post-install survey submissions
- See [Admin Surveys (Customer Feedback)](#admin-surveys-customer-feedback)

### Users Activity (`/admin/users-activity`)
- Sales rep grid, per-rep activity dialog, and company-wide activity table
- See [Admin Users Activity (Sales Rep & Staff Tracking)](#admin-users-activity-sales-rep--staff-tracking)

### Invoices (`/admin/invoices`)
- Invoice listing and per-sale invoice view

### Instructions (Admin)
- Add, edit, delete, and reorder instructions
- **Visible to** position toggles control which staff positions see each instruction on the employee page and in AI Chat Instructions mode
- See [Admin Instructions (Knowledge Base & Position Visibility)](#admin-instructions-knowledge-base--position-visibility)

### Teach Mode & Employee Progress
- Admin teach-mode management
- `/admin/employee-progress` — Staff training progress

### Company & Users (`/admin/company`, `/admin/users`)
- Sidebar: **Company settings** → **Company** or **Users** (not a standalone top-level Company link)
- See [Admin Company Settings & Users](#admin-company-settings--users) — includes [Adding or changing the company logo](#adding-or-changing-the-company-logo)

### SMS (`/admin/cloudtalk` or `/admin/ringcentral`)
- Read-only oversight of SMS threads (no send, no **Mark as unread**, no **New conversation**)
- Employee send mode is documented in [Employee SMS](#employee-sms)

## Admin Stones (Stone / Material Management)

Use this area to build and maintain your shop’s stone catalog: granite, quartz, marble, dolomite, and quartzite colors, pricing, photos, color tags, price tiers (levels), and individual slabs in stock.

**Where to find it:** Sign in as Admin → sidebar **Inventory** → **Stones**. The catalog opens at `/admin/stones`.

---

### Browsing the stone catalog

#### Grid view and table view

At the top of the page you can switch layouts:

- **Grid view** — Photo cards with name, availability, size, price, and bundle number (when set). Best for visual browsing.
- **Table view** — Sortable columns: image, name, type, size, available count, amount, retail price, cost per square foot, and actions.

Your last chosen view is remembered for your next visit.

#### How stones are ordered on screen

The catalog groups stones automatically:

1. **In stock and set to Display** — shown first, sorted A–Z by name.
2. **Out of stock but still set to Display** — shown next (may show an “Out of Stock” label on the photo).
3. **Not set to Display** — shown last and appear faded (dimmed) so you can tell they are hidden from the customer-facing catalog.

Stones without a photo still appear, but they sort with the groups above based on stock and display settings.

#### Sidebar filters

With **Stones** selected in the sidebar, expand the filter panel under Inventory:

| Filter | What it does |
|--------|----------------|
| **Type** | Show only selected material types from your company’s configured list. You can pick more than one. |
| **Show sold out** | When on, includes stones that have no available slabs. When off, sold-out items may be hidden from the list. |
| **Supplier** | Limit to stones tied to a specific vendor. |
| **Color** | Limit to stones tagged with one or more color groups (e.g. white, gray, brown). |
| **Level** | Limit to price tiers 1 through 7. |
| **Finishing** | Limit to Polished, Leathered, or Honed. |

Changing a filter refreshes the catalog. Use **Clear** next to a filter group to reset that group.

#### Stone search

Use the **Stone Search** box at the top right. As you type, matching stones appear in a dropdown with name, price, and stock status. From search you can:

- Open the stone’s **slab list** (click the result).
- Jump to **Edit** (admin actions in the search dropdown).
- Start **Delete**.

Admin search includes sold-out stones so you can still find and edit them.

#### Opening a stone from the catalog

- **Click the card or table row** — Opens a popup listing all **slabs** for that stone (bundle numbers, sizes, sold vs available). You can click a slab photo to enlarge it and click slab dimensions to edit length × width when needed.
- **Pencil icon (grid)** or **Edit in the actions menu (table)** — Opens the **Edit Stone** dialog on the **General** tab.
- **X icon (grid)** or **Delete in the actions menu (table)** — Starts the delete flow.

---

### Adding a new stone

1. On the catalog page, click **Add Stone**.
2. Fill in the **Add Stone** form (see [Field rules](#field-rules-for-stones) below).
3. Click **Add Stone** at the bottom.

#### Adding and managing stone types

The **Type** list is managed separately for each company, so you can use material categories that match your inventory.

1. Open **Add Stone**.
2. Open **Type** and choose **Manage Types**.
3. In **Manage Stone Types**:
   - Enter a name and click **Add** to create a type.
   - Click the pencil beside a type to rename it. Renaming also updates existing stones that use that type.
   - Click the trash icon to delete an unused type.
4. Close the manager, open **Type**, and select the type for the new stone.

Type names are required, can contain up to 255 characters, and cannot duplicate another company type. A type used by an existing stone cannot be deleted.

**What happens when you save:**

- The new stone is created for your company with the name, type, finishing, pricing, dimensions, supplier, level, color tags, bundle number, and display settings you entered.
- The **main photo** you uploaded becomes the stone’s catalog image.
- Any **colors** you selected are saved as tags on that stone (used for sidebar color filtering).
- You see a success message and a short confirmation dialog: **“Stone Added”**.
- The catalog reloads with **Show sold out** turned on so the new entry is easy to find even before slabs exist.

**Add slabs now?**

The confirmation dialog asks whether you want to add slabs immediately:

- **Yes, add slabs** — Takes you straight to **Edit Stone → Slabs** for the new stone.
- **No, I'm done** — Returns you to the catalog.

You can add slabs later anytime via **Edit Stone → Slabs**.

---

### Editing a stone

Open edit from the pencil icon, table actions, or stone search. The **Edit Stone** dialog has three tabs:

#### General tab

Update the same fields as when adding a stone (name, type, photo, toggles, supplier, size, pricing, level, finishing, colors, bundle number).

**What happens when you save:**

- All general fields are updated on the existing stone record.
- **Photo:** If you upload a new image, it replaces the old catalog photo and the previous image file is removed from storage. If you leave the image unchanged, the current photo stays.
- **Colors:** Your color selections replace the previous tags entirely (old color links are cleared, then the new set is saved).
- The dialog closes and you return to the catalog with a **“Stone Edited”** success message. Your current filters stay applied.

#### Images tab

Manage **additional installed-stone photos** (kitchen installs, showroom samples, etc.) beyond the main catalog image.

- **Upload** — Add one or more images; each appears in a grid on this tab.
- **Delete** — Remove an individual extra image (trash icon on the image).
- **Link Images from Different Stone** — Pick another stone that already has install photos; those images are **linked** here so you do not re-upload duplicates. Linked images appear in a **Linked Images** section grouped by source stone name.
- **Unlink** — Removes the link to another stone’s images without deleting the originals on the source stone.

#### Slabs tab

Manage **individual slabs in inventory** for this stone.

**Add a slab**

1. Enter **Bundle** (slab number or label — required).
2. Optionally attach a **slab photo**.
3. Enter **Length** and **Width** (defaults to the stone’s general length/width if you leave them blank or zero).
4. Click **Add Slab**.

Each saved slab appears in the list with its number, size, and thumbnail. Slab photos are optional; if omitted, the stone’s main catalog image is used as the thumbnail.

**Edit a slab number**

Click the pencil next to a slab, change the bundle label, and confirm with the checkmark (or press Enter). Empty labels cannot be saved.

**Delete a slab**

Click **X** on a slab, confirm in the dialog. The slab is **removed from active inventory** (hidden from lists). It is not permanently erased from history.

**Link slabs from another stone**

Use **Link Slabs from Different Stone** to reuse another stone’s slab list (for example, two catalog entries that share the same physical bundles). Pick a stone from the searchable list and confirm **Link Slabs**. Linked slabs appear under **Linked Slabs**, grouped by source stone. Use **Unlink** to stop showing them on this stone without deleting slabs on the source stone.

You cannot link a stone to itself or link the same source twice. Stones that already link to each other in conflicting ways are excluded from the picker.

---

### Deleting a stone

Start delete from the **X** on a grid card, the table actions menu, or stone search.

**Step 1 — Confirm name**

You are asked: *Are you sure you want to delete [stone name]?*

- **Cancel** — Closes the dialog; nothing changes.
- **Confirm** — If the stone has **no active slabs**, it is deleted immediately. If it **has active slabs**, you go to step 2.

**Step 2 — Slabs warning (only when slabs exist)**

You see how many slabs are still associated. The message explains that the stone and its slabs will be **hidden from inventory** — nothing is permanently wiped from the system.

- **Back** — Returns to step 1.
- **Confirm** — Hides the stone and marks its slabs as removed from active inventory. Slab image files may be cleaned up from storage.

After deletion you return to the catalog with a **“Stone Deleted”** message. The stone no longer appears in normal catalog views.

Use these rules when adding or editing on the **General** tab.

| Field | Required? | Rules and notes |

When you upload or replace a stone **Main photo** on **Add** or **Edit** (General tab), a crop dialog opens. This is the **only** place in the app with brightness, contrast, and per-channel color sliders.

1. Choose the image file on the General tab.
2. In the crop dialog, drag the corner handles to crop the image.
3. Adjust sliders if needed:
   - **Brightness**
   - **Contrast**
   - **Red**, **Green**, **Blue**
4. Click **Save** in the dialog to apply crop and adjustments.
5. Click **Save** on the stone form to store the stone.

**Not available elsewhere:** **Resources > Images** (Admin or Employee) has **no** brightness, contrast, or color controls — only name and file upload/replace.
| **Display** | No (default **On**) | When **Off**, the stone is hidden from customer/showroom views and appears faded in your admin catalog. |
| **On Sale** | No (default **Off**) | Marks the stone as on sale for filtering and display logic. |
| **Regular Stock** | No (default **Off**) | When **On**, the stone can show as **“Regular Stock”** in availability even when no numbered slabs are counted — use for materials you always carry. |

|-------|-----------|--------|

### Understanding availability labels

When reading the catalog or slab popup, you may see:

| Label | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| **Regular Stock** | **Regular Stock** is enabled and no whole slabs are counted, but the material is still treated as available. |
| **Remnants Only** | No full slabs left, but partial/remnant inventory exists. |
| **Out of Stock** | No available quantity and not regular stock. |
| **Count (e.g. 3 / 5)** | Whole slabs available vs total whole slabs for that stone. |
| **Faded card** | **Display** is off — hidden from customer-facing catalog. |

Sold slabs in the slab popup are highlighted in **red**; partial pieces linked to a parent sale may show in **yellow**. Hover or view tooltips on sold slabs for sale date, customer, seller, and notes when that data exists.

### Typical workflow for inventory staff

1. **Add stone** — Name, type, photo, pricing, level, colors, supplier, finishing.
2. **Add slabs** — One row per physical slab with bundle number (and optional slab photo).
3. **Tune visibility** — Turn **Display** on for showroom; turn off for discontinued colors.
4. **Maintain** — Edit prices and levels on **General**; add install photos on **Images**; remove sold slabs on **Slabs**.
5. **Retire** — Delete the stone when it should leave the catalog entirely (confirm slab cleanup if needed).

## Admin Surveys (Customer Feedback)

Use this page to **read** customer feedback after installation. Surveys are filled out by customers on a public form; admins do not create or edit survey responses here.

**Where to find it:** Sign in as Admin → sidebar **Survey** → `/admin/surveys`.

**Page title:** Customer Surveys

---

### How customers receive the survey

After an installer submits a **post-install checklist**, the system can notify the customer automatically:

1. **Email** — If the checklist includes a customer email, an email is sent with subject `[Company name] - Post-Installation Survey` and a link to the survey.
2. **SMS** — If the company has CloudTalk enabled, a customer phone is on file, and an **Office Manager** user has a **CloudTalk phone number** set, an SMS is sent from that Office Manager line with the same survey link.

The survey URL format is:

`/customer/{companyId}/survey`

Example: `/customer/3/survey` for company ID 3.

You can also share this link manually (for example in a follow-up email). Admins can preview the customer showroom from the sidebar **Customer** button; the survey is part of that public customer area.

---

### Customer survey form (what they fill out)

The public form states the survey is **fully anonymous**. Required fields:

| Section | What the customer provides |
|---------|---------------------------|
| **Pick your sales rep** | Dropdown of active **Sales Representative** users for that company |
| **How did you like the sales rep?** | Star rating 1–5 (required) and optional comments |
| **How did you like the template technician?** | Star rating 1–5 (required) and optional comments |
| **Pick your installer** | Dropdown of active **Installer** users for that company |
| **How did you like the installation team?** | Star rating 1–5 (required) and optional comments |

After **Submit**, the form shows a green thank-you message and disables further edits. If required fields are missing, the customer sees an error banner.

Staff who appear in the dropdowns must have the correct position assigned in **Admin → Users** (Sales Representative or Installer).

---

### Viewing submissions on the admin page

The admin page shows a **card grid** (two columns on wider screens), newest first.

Each card includes:

| Area | Content |
|------|---------|
| **Header** | Sales rep name, installer name, submission date |
| **Sales rep** | Rating out of 5 and optional comment |
| **Technician** | Rating out of 5 and optional comment |
| **Installation team** | Rating out of 5 and optional comment |

If a name was not stored, the card shows **Sales rep not specified** or **Not specified** for the installer.

The sales rep and installer names printed on these cards come from the staff user accounts. To correct or change an installer name, a sales rep name, or a technician name, edit that person's **Name** in **Admin → Company settings → Users → Actions → Edit** (a Manager with Admin access can do this). Cards for surveys that were already submitted keep the name stored at submission time.

When no surveys exist yet, the page shows **No surveys found.**

There is no search, filter, export, or delete on this page — it is a read-only feedback inbox.

---

### Typical workflow for managers

1. Ensure installers complete **checklists** in the field so customers receive the survey link by email/SMS.
2. Confirm **Sales Representative** and **Installer** positions are assigned correctly so customers can pick the right names.
3. Review **Admin → Survey** weekly for low ratings or recurring complaints in the comment fields.
4. Follow up offline with the sales rep or installation team as needed (the survey does not trigger internal alerts).

### How to see how many calls a sales rep made

There is **no Call history button**, **no Call history tab**, and **no separate call-history page** on Users Activity. Phone calls appear only inside each rep’s activity dialog.

1. Go to **Admin → Users Activity** (Admin access required).
2. In the **Sales rep selector** grid at the top, click the **sales rep’s name button** for the person whose calls you want to review.
3. The **`[Name] activity`** dialog opens. While CloudTalk data loads, you may briefly see **Loading call history...** — that is a status message, not a button.
4. In the dialog table, find rows whose **Type of activity** is **Made a call**, **Received a call**, or **Missed a call**. Each row is one call (grouped rows show a count, e.g. `Made a call (3)`).

Calls load only for reps who have a **CloudTalk agent ID** set in **Admin → Company settings → Users → Edit**. Reps without an agent ID still open in the dialog, but no call rows will appear for them.

Missed and inbound calls are attributed to the CloudTalk agent on the call. An inbound call that rang a group and was never assigned to an agent does not show up under any single rep.

## Employee Deals (Deal Board & Pipeline)

Use the deal board to track your sales pipeline: move customers through stages, log activities, attach files, email from the deal, and mark deals won or lost.

**Where to find it:** Sign in as Employee → sidebar **CRM** → **Deals**. The board opens at `/employee/deals`.

**What you see:** Only deals assigned to **you** (your user account). Other employees’ deals do not appear on your board.

---

### Browsing the deal board

#### Toolbar filters

At the top of the board:

| Control | What it does |
|---------|----------------|
| **Group** | Switches which deal board layout you are viewing. Each group has its own set of stage columns. A red alert icon on a group means that group has overdue activities on at least one deal. |
| **Status** | Filters which deals appear: **Active Deals** (open pipeline), **Won**, or **Lost**. |
| **Add Deal** | Opens the create-deal dialog (desktop toolbar button; on mobile, use the ⋮ menu → **Add New Deal**). |

Your current group and status filter stay in the URL, so refreshing or sharing the link keeps the same view.

#### Stage columns

The board is a row of **columns** (lists). Each column is a pipeline stage (for example *New Customer*, *Quoted*, *Template*). The column header shows the stage name and how many deals are in that column.

Stages and groups are configured by Admin. Employees use the board as set up for the company; changing column names or adding/removing stages is done in Admin under **Deals → Manage lists**.

#### How deals are sorted in a column

Within each column, deals sort automatically:

1. Deals **without** an upcoming activity appear first (newest deal on top).
2. Deals **with** an upcoming activity sort by nearest activity deadline (soonest first).

#### Deal cards

Each card shows:

- **Customer name** (and company name when set) — click to open the deal.
- **Title** — optional text shown **directly under the customer name** in smaller gray text on the card. Teams often use this for a **job site address** or short location label so it is visible on the board without opening the deal.
- **Amount** — click the dollar amount on the card to edit inline.
- **Nearest activity** — name of the next open task; click to open the deal on that activity. If there is no activity, the card shows *No upcoming activities* in red.
- **Activity deadline** — colored pill (overdue, today, upcoming). Click to change the date on the card.
- **Icons** — paperclip (images), mail (email linked to deal), clipboard (open activities), note (notes).
- **Sales rep** — shown in the corner when set on the customer.
- **Lost reason** — shown on lost deals when recorded.

On **mobile**, swipe horizontally to move between columns. While dragging a deal, the board can auto-scroll to the next column when you drag near the screen edge.

#### Find Customer

Below the toolbar, **Find Customer** searches customers on your board (your deals only). Selecting a customer **highlights** their deal card and scrolls it into view. If the deal is on another group or won/lost view, the board switches filter automatically and then highlights the card.

From search you can also jump to **Edit** or **Delete** for that customer’s deal when one exists.

---

### Moving deals between stages

**Drag and drop** a deal card from one column to another to change its stage.

- On desktop, click and drag the card (not the customer name link).
- On touch devices, press and hold briefly, then drag.

When you drop a deal in a new column:

- The deal’s stage updates immediately on screen.
- Stage history is recorded for reporting.
- If the deal was **Won** or **Lost** and you move it to another active column, it is **reactivated** (returned to active pipeline) and any lost reason is cleared.

You can also change stage indirectly from the deal’s **General** tab (saved list/stage) or from **Project** when moving the deal to another **Group** (see below).

### Adding a deal

1. Click **Add Deal** (or mobile **Add New Deal**).
2. In **Create Deal**:
   - **Customer** — search and select an existing customer (required). You can create a customer from the search if needed.
   - **Amount** — optional dollar value.
   - **Title** — optional label shown under the customer name on the board (often a job site address).
3. Click **Create**.

**What happens when you save:**

- A new deal is created for the selected customer in the **first column** of the current board view (based on the active group and `list_id` in the URL).
- The deal is owned by **you**.
- Initial stage name matches the column the deal was placed in.
- If you are a **sales rep**, creating the deal may assign you as that customer’s sales rep (when they had no rep or a different rep).
- You return to the board with a success message.

### Opening a deal

Click the **customer name** on a card (or use Find Customer → Edit). The **Edit Deal** dialog opens over the board.

At the top:

- **Progress bar** — shows every stage in the current group, which stage the deal is in, and how long it spent in each stage.
- **Close** — returns to the board (your group/status filters are preserved).

#### Showing an address on the deal board

Deals do **not** have a separate address field. To make an address (or any short location text) **visible on the deal card**:

1. Open **Deals** and click the deal (customer name on the card).
2. Go to the **General** tab (not Project).
3. Enter the address (or site label) in **Title**.
4. Click **Save**.

After save, the text appears on the board **below the customer name** on that deal’s card.

**Two different “addresses” to know:**

| Goal | Where to set it | Where it shows |
|------|-----------------|----------------|
| Address visible **on the board card** | **General** tab → **Title** | Under customer name on the deal card |
| Customer’s real mailing/project address | **Customers** → edit customer | **Project** tab on the deal (read-only table); map and copy buttons |

Use **Title** when installers or sales reps need to spot the job location from the Kanban board. Use the **customer address** when you need the full contact record, maps, or email templates tied to the customer.

#### Recording deal value or invoice amounts

Deals do **not** have a separate **invoice amount** field. How to track money on a deal depends on what you need:

| Goal | What to use | Steps |
|------|-------------|--------|
| Dollar value on the **pipeline / board card** | **Amount** | **Deals** → open deal → **General** → **Amount** → **Save**. Or click the amount on the card and edit inline. |
| Extra billing detail (quote vs invoice, line items, “invoiced $X on date”) | **Deal notes** | Open deal → activity panel → **Notes** tab → **Write a note...** → **Add Note**. |
| Official invoices after a **sale** is completed | **Admin → Invoices** | Lists sales transactions; open a sale for per-sale invoice view. This is separate from the deal board — it applies once a sale exists, not while editing an open deal. |

If you asked for an “invoice amount” on an active deal, use **Amount** when you want one number on the card, or a **note** when you need more context than a single dollar field allows.

### Selling a slab (step by step)

There are two ways to start a sale:

#### A. Sell from a specific slab

1. Open the stone’s slab list.
2. Click **Sell** on an available (white) slab.
3. The **Sell Slab - Add Customer** dialog opens with that slab pre-added to Room 1.

#### B. Sell Slab from the catalog toolbar

1. On `/employee/stones`, click **Sell Slab**.
2. The same dialog opens with an empty room — add slabs manually (see below).

#### Fill in the sale form

**Customer & project**

| Field | Required? | Notes |
|-------|-----------|--------|
| **Customer** | Yes | Search and select. You can create a customer from search if needed. |
| **Project address same as billing address** | No | Toggle on by default. Turn off to enter a separate project address. |
| **Seller** | Yes (defaults to you) | Dropdown of sales reps. |

**Rooms** — each sale has one or more rooms (kitchen, bathroom, etc.):

| Field | Required? | Notes |
|-------|-----------|--------|
| **Room** | Yes | Kitchen, Bathroom, Outdoor, Island, or custom |
| **Square Feet** | Yes | Must be greater than zero |
| **Stone Search** | No | Pick a stone to auto-fill retail pricing for the room |

Per room, use the **Slabs**, **Sinks**, and **Faucets** tabs:

**Slabs tab**

- **Add Slab** — pick additional slabs from inventory.
- Each slab row shows bundle label and **Full Slab Sold** toggle:
  - **On (Full)** — entire physical slab is sold; row shows red **(Full)** badge.
  - **Off (Partial)** — only part of the slab is sold; row shows yellow **(Partial)** badge. After submit, the system keeps a **remnant** child slab in inventory for the unused portion.
- Remove extra slabs with **X** (at least one slab per room is required).

**Sinks tab** — **Add Sink**, set price per sink, remove with **X**.

**Faucets tab** — **Add Faucet**, set price per faucet, remove with **X**.

**Multiple rooms** — click **Add Room** at the bottom of the form. Remove Room 2+ with the **X** on the room header.

**Notes** — optional **Notes to Sale** at the bottom.

#### Submit the sale

Click **Submit**.

**What happens:**

- A **sale (transaction)** is created with status **pending**.
- Slabs are linked to the sale; sold rows turn **red** on the slab list.
- Partial sales create **child remnant** slabs (yellow) still in stock.
- If the customer had no sales rep, the **seller** may be assigned as their rep.
- Success toast: **Sale completed successfully**.
- You return to the slab list (or catalog) with the sale recorded.

**Validation errors:**

- Customer required.
- Each room needs at least one slab.
- Each room needs square feet greater than zero.

### Editing a transaction (shop floor)

**Dialog title:** Transaction Details

#### Sale information (top)

Read-only summary: **Customer**, **Sale Date**, **Sold By**, **Project Address**.

#### Rooms and slabs (main work area)

Slabs are grouped by **room** (Kitchen, Bathroom, etc.). Each room shows:

- Room name (editable for newly added empty rooms)
- **Total sqft per room** — click pencil to edit square feet for the room
- Table per room: **Bundle**, **Stone**, **Status** (Cut / Uncut), **Notes**, **Cut Date**, **Actions**

**Per-slab Actions menu (⋮):**

| Action | When available | What it does |
|--------|----------------|--------------|
| **Cut** | Slab is uncut | Marks slab cut; clears unused child remnants tied to that slab |
| **Uncut** | Slab is cut | Reverses cut status (shop floor correction) |
| **Partial** | Slab is uncut | Opens **Mark as partially cut** — enter leftover **Length** and **Width** |
| **Replace** | Slab is uncut | Swap slab for another available bundle from inventory |
| **Remove** | More than one slab on sale | Remove slab from this transaction (cannot remove the last slab) |

**Mark as partially cut dialog:**

- Enter leftover dimensions for the remnant piece.
- **More left overs** — save this piece and cut again for another remnant.
- **Save** (or equivalent submit) — finish partial cut for this step.

Uncut slabs show a **green** badge; cut slabs show **blue** with cut date.

#### Add slab

**Add Slab** button (bottom):

1. Choose **room** (existing or new room name).
2. Search for a **stone**.
3. Pick an available **bundle** from inventory.
4. Confirm add — slab joins the sale in that room.

#### Sinks

Second card lists sinks on the sale with types and prices (read-only in this view).

#### Close

**Close** returns to `/shop/transactions` with filters preserved.

### Typical shop workflow

1. Set **Status** to **In Progress** and optionally filter by **Sales Rep**.
2. Find the job by customer, bundle, or stone (table or search).
3. Open the transaction.
4. For each room, mark slabs **Cut** when fabrication is done, or **Partial** when a remnant remains.
5. Use **Replace** if the shop must swap to a different bundle before cutting.
6. Use **Add Slab** if the sale gains an extra slab during production.
7. **Close** and move to the next job.

When every slab on a sale is cut, status moves toward **Cut** on the list. **Installed** and payroll steps are handled outside this shop screen (e.g. employee/admin **Transactions** with **Mark as Installed**).

## User positions & access

Each user in the system has one or more **positions** that determine which pages they can reach. An admin user (`is_admin`) can see the Admin portal; an employee user (`is_employee`) can see the Employee portal. Some positions lock a user into a single-purpose portal regardless of those flags.

| Position | Portal / Access | Key pages |
|----------|----------------|-----------|
| **Sales Rep** | Employee CRM. Cannot be combined with Shop Worker. | Inventory, CRM (Customers, Deals, Emails), Sinks, Faucets, Resources, Operations, My Account, Samples, Checklists |
| **Sales Manager** | Same as Sales Rep, plus Delete on Customers list, Telegram lead alerts, lead assignment | Same as Sales Rep |
| **Shop Manager** | Label only — access depends on whether paired with Employee or Admin | — |
| **Shop Worker** | Shop app only. Cannot be combined with Sales Rep. | Transactions, Samples, My Account (`/shop/user`) |
| **Manager** | Label only. When paired with Admin, unlocks **Company settings**: Users and Company pages | Admin > Company settings > Users, Admin > Company settings > Company (tax rate, logo, address) |
| **Installer** | Checklist form only | `/installers/:companyId/checklist` |
| **Marketing** | External Marketing portal only | Leads, Add lead, Edit lead, Delete lead, walk-in stats, deal-by-stage summary |
| **Walk-in** | Walk-in form only | `/customer/:companyId/check-in` |
| **Super Admin** | Admin and employee access in each assigned company. Can switch companies from the header. **Users**, **Company**, and **Billing** still need the Manager position, which only applies in the home company. Only a platform superuser can edit or delete a Super Admin. | Employee + Admin pages for each assigned company |
| **Office Manager** | Employee CRM label. With a CloudTalk phone set, post-install survey links are also sent by SMS from that number. | — |
| **Template Guy** | Employee CRM label for template technicians. Only used to choose who sees an Instruction (**Visible to**). | — |

**Position + flag combinations matter:**
- A user with the **Manager** position and `is_admin = true` sees **Admin > Company settings > Users** and **Admin > Company settings > Company** in the sidebar. Without the Manager position, even an admin cannot see those pages.
- **Marketing** users are redirected to `/external/marketing/:companyId/leads` on login and cannot reach the Employee or Admin portals.
- **Shop Worker** users are redirected to `/shop/transactions` and cannot reach the Employee CRM.
- If a user has more than one portal position, the first of **Installer**, **Walk-in**, **Marketing**, **Shop Worker** decides where they land.
- Platform superuser and **Super Admin** accounts can only be edited or deleted by a platform superuser.
